Order 
The instant misc. miscellaneous petition under Article 227 of the Constitution of India has been filed by petitioner-claimant assailing the order dated 23.07.2025 passed by learned Fourth Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jaura, District Morena (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal")
in Claim Case No.26/2024, whereby petitioner's application under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the claim petition by substituting Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 in place of Section 164, has been rejected.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation for injuries sustained in a road accident that occurred on 04.08.2023.

It was pleaded that while petitioner was returning from Bilgaon to Sanjay Nagar and reached near C.M. Sunrise NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28235 2 MP-4058-2025 School, a motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-06-MZ-1857, driven rashly and negligently by respondent No.2, dashed against him, causing grievous injuries resulting in permanent disability.
During the course of proceedings, the petitioner realized that due to a typographical error, the claim was filed under Section 164 instead of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Accordingly, an application under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC was moved seeking correction of the said mistake.
The same was opposed by the respondent No.3-Insurance Company and was ultimately dismissed by the learned Claims Tribunal vide impugned order dated 23.07.2025.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation enacted to provide just compensation to victims of road accidents.
Therefore, a mere clerical or typographical error in mentioning the statutory provision should not defeat the claimant's substantive right.
It was further urged that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability and has adduced evidence to that effect; hence, the rejection of amendment was unjustified.
4. Conversely, learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company supported the impugned order and prayed for dismissal of petition.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record, this Court finds that the learned Claims Tribunal erred in adopting a hyper- technical approach.

The Motor Vehicles Act,
being a piece of social welfare legislation, must be interpreted liberally in favour of the victim/injured/claimant.

A bona fide typographical mistake in quoting the wrong Section should not defeat the ends of justice, especially when the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:28235 3 MP-4058-2025 nature of claim and cause of action remain the same and no prejudice is caused to the opposite party.
6.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 23.07.2025 passed by the Claims Tribunal is set aside.
The application filed by petitioner under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC is hereby allowed.

The learned Claims Tribunal is directed to permit the petitioner- claimant to amend the claim petition by substituting Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act in place of Section 164 and to decide the claim petition on merits in accordance with law after affording opportunity of hearing to both sides.
